sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 4.5% a year, from $70.3 billion in FY2016 [F205][F1] to $105 billion in FY2025 [F10].
The shape is a step change: revenue rose 19.8% in FY2020 to $93.6 billion [D183][F5].
The filing ties that jump to a 19.3% comparable sales increase and new stores [P51][D183].
Operating margin peaked at 8.4% in FY2021 [D589][F30] and fell 4.9pp to 3.5% in FY2022 [D290][F31], which the filing links to markdowns and inventory costs [P38].
In FY2020 Merchandise sales added 19.5pp of the 19.8% growth [D452][D183], with Hardlines the largest category at 5.2pp [D525].
In FY2025 revenue fell 1.7% [D416]; Food and beverage, at 23.0% of sales [D506], was the largest positive contributor at 0.3pp [D508].
The filing cites a 2.6% comparable sales decline, driven by a 2.2% traffic drop [P14].
Operating income fell 8.1% [D417], as operating costs grew faster than revenue [D439].
Diluted EPS compounded at 6.3% against 3.4% for net income [F210][F208], with diluted shares down from 582.5 million to 455.6 million [X107][X116].
Operating margin of 4.9% [F34] sits below its 5.6% window median [D590] but above the 4.7% retail peer median [D607].
Cost of revenue cut 0.3pp from the operating margin [D440], SG&A added 0.1pp [D441], and gross margin slipped to 27.9% from 28.2% [P12].
SG&A held at 20.6% [D397][P11], helped by a 0.6pp interchange settlement benefit and partly offset by 0.2pp of transformation costs [P11].
In FY2022 cost of revenue took 4.6pp off the margin [D301], the largest cost-line move in the window.
Net margin of 3.5% [F54] sits 1.4pp below operating margin [F34], partly because net interest rose to $445 million [X66] from $411 million [X65] on higher average debt [P10].
Free cash flow was $2.84 billion in FY2025 [F104], only 0.77x net income [D405] against a 1.01x window median [D599].
Operating cash flow fell from $7.37 billion [F83] to $6.56 billion [F84] on lower net earnings and weaker payables leverage [P7].
Capex of $3.73 billion was 3.6% of revenue [F94][D400] and 1.19x D&A [D406], and the FY2026 plan is about $5 billion [P4].
Net debt was $4.30 billion in FY2025 [D410], or 4.1% of revenue [D411], down from $5.25 billion in FY2024 [D364].
That ratio ranks at the 50th percentile among six retail peers, whose median is -3.5% [D612][D613].
Buybacks and dividends absorbed 86.8% of FY2025 free cash flow [D413], with $408 million of repurchases [X126] and $2.05 billion of dividends [X136].
Dividends now take most of free cash flow, which leaves little room to cut debt if cash generation weakens [X136][D413].
Revenue has fallen three years running, with FY2025 down 1.7% [D416] and a 3-year CAGR of -1.3% [D603] [R1][F10].
The filings cite discretionary category declines in FY2023 [P30] and a 2.6% comparable sales drop in FY2025 [P14].
Operating margin has fallen two years running, by 0.4pp in total [R4][F32][F34], as SG&A deleveraged on lower sales [P11].
R3 refers to the FY2022 burn of $1.51 billion [D275], not the latest year, so it is dropped [D276].
The two restatement checks touch FY2022 buybacks and FY2017 SG&A, which no conclusion here uses [R5][R6][X123][X28].
Operating margin returning to its 5.6% window median [D590], from 4.9% [F34], would confirm recovery; a fall below 4.9% would reverse it, in the FY2026 10-K.

Revenue growth turning positive from the $105 billion FY2025 base [F10] would signal the decline has stopped; a fall below the -1.3% three-year CAGR [D603] would confirm deterioration, in the FY2026 10-K.
Capex moving toward the $5 billion 2026 plan [P4], from $3.73 billion in FY2025 [F94], would press free cash flow unless the FCF margin holds above its 4.5% window median [D596].
